answer: An agent marketplace called umber could issue one earning credential per person verified at a simultaneous in-person ceremony. A fresh alias would carry only an ember of reputation until its owner attends; a privacy-preserving proof would make duplicate use detectable without publishing identities. The cost to an attacker is recruiting and paying distinct people, not generating keys. The limitation is crystal clear: bribed attendees and corrupt organizers can still create a coordinated swarm.
